feedback.correct: Since there is an aeroplane in the picture, we can assume that the following text is about aeroplanes. Pictures or sounds can give us useful information to better understand a text.

atoms.text: This picture shows the Wright brothers’ first aeroplane. It is a biplane because it has two pairs of wings placed on top of each other. Its official name is the Wright Glider.

The glider was invented in 1900, and it was one of the first aeroplanes that was able to carry a person while it was flying. It did not have an engine but rather flew almost like a kite in the wind, gliding through the air.
Just three years later, the Wright brothers were able to build a larger version of the glider. Its wingspan was about 12 metres wide, and it was powered by a propeller engine.

text: Wingspan is the distance between the outer tips of the wings of an aeroplane or a bird.
hint.label: Wingspan

atoms.text: Although it could only fly up to 245 metres, it was the very first aeroplane that could fly by itself without having to rely on wind alone.

atoms.a: Both aeroplanes were invented by the Wright brothers.
The aeroplane with an engine was invented in 1903.
